content.content:
[toolchain]
channel = "stable"
components = [
    "clippy",
    "rustfmt",
]
# Default recipe: fast local CI pipeline (no coverage) via moon & just.
# Use `just ci` explicitly for full CI parity including coverage.
default: ci

# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
build:
    moon run :build

# Build release CLI binary
build-release:
    cargo build --release -p callisto-cli

# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests. This intentionally uses the
# same Nextest command as CI: a runner/configuration failure must never be
# mistaken for a passing Moon fallback.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Explicit compatibility path for contributors who do not have cargo-nextest
# installed. It is never used by CI or pre-merge verification.
test-moon:
    moon run :test
    cargo test --doc --workspace

# Exercise the Release-PR action's real shell block with Git and GitHub API
# boundaries faked. This proves the script's control flow given a decision
# shape; it does not call the real `callisto` binary, so it cannot catch a
# mismatch between what Callisto actually serializes and what this script's
# jq expressions expect. See test-release-action-binary for that check.
test-release-action:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh

# Compiles callisto and runs the Release-PR action's jq extraction against
# its real JSON output. Requires pending changesets to exercise update and
# supersede decisions; skips cleanly otherwise.
test-release-action-binary:
    bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_decide_binary_contract.sh

# Execute the release lifecycle at the real CLI boundary with fake registry,
# Git, forge, and attestation providers. This is deliberately separate from
# broad workspace tests so PR CI makes the release behavior evidence visible.
release-workflow-behavior:
    bash .github/tests/release-workflow-behavior/run.sh

# Re-captures the real provider responses under testing/fixtures/providers with
# read-only network GETs. Manual: review the diff and update PROVENANCE.md.
provider-fixtures:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh

# Manual and network-dependent, so deliberately not part of `ci`: re-fetches the
# live providers and asserts each fixture's SHAPE (status code, JSON key paths,
# ls-remote line kinds) still matches; content is never compared.
provider-contract:
    bash testing/refresh-provider-fixtures.sh --check

# Run Clippy lints (warnings treated as errors) as a single workspace invocation.
# Moon's per-project `cargo clippy -p $project` tasks all lock the same shared
# target/ dir, so running them one-per-project serializes on Cargo's own build
# lock instead of parallelizing — a single --workspace invocation lets Cargo's
# internal job scheduler parallelize across crates instead.
lint:
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used

# Lint only projects affected by changes since the base branch. Uses moon's
# project graph to find affected crates, then lints them in one cargo
# invocation (not moon's per-project fan-out) to avoid Cargo's build-lock
# serialization while still skipping unaffected crates entirely.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --lib --bins -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used

# Check code formatting compliance via moon
fmt-check:
    moon run :format-check

# Format code automatically via moon
fmt:
    moon run :format

# Security advisory, ban, license & source check via cargo-deny (workspace root, one pass)
audit: license-boundary
    cargo deny check

# callisto-model is MIT: nothing it depends on at build or run time, directly or not, may be FSL-licensed or a Callisto FSL crate.
license-boundary:
    ! cargo tree -p callisto-model -e normal,build --prefix none --format '{p} {l}' | grep -E 'FSL|callisto-(manifests|graph|cli|fixtures)'

# Compile the fuzz targets so they cannot rot (running them needs nightly and cargo-fuzz)
fuzz-check:
    cargo check --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml --bins

# Run mutation testing sweep via cargo-mutants
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Run unused dependency check via cargo-machete
machete:
    cargo machete

# Verify public Rust API SemVer breaking changes
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Run structure-aware fuzzing target
fuzz target="parse_package_id":
    cargo fuzz run {{target}}

# Documentation build check (warnings treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace

# Generate code coverage report via cargo-llvm-cov.
#
# Optional `threshold`: when set, fails if total line coverage drops below
# it (--fail-under-lines). The human-readable summary is always emitted
# before enforcing the threshold: LCOV output itself contains no aggregate
# percentage, and a failed CI gate must say what developers need to improve.
# Unset means informational only; `just ci` and CI both call `just coverage 90`,
# so a CI coverage failure always reproduces locally with the same invocation.
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    args=(--workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info)
    cargo llvm-cov "${args[@]}"
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{threshold}}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{threshold}}"
    fi

# Check per-crate line coverage against a threshold (default 90%). The
# workspace-total --fail-under-lines gate can pass while a small crate is
# far below threshold, since a few large crates dominate the total line
# count -- this catches that case. Requires profile data from a prior
# `cargo llvm-cov` run in this session (e.g. `just coverage` just ran, or
# CI's own coverage step ran first); does not re-run tests itself.
coverage-per-crate threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov report --json --summary-only > /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json
    report=$(jq -r '
        .data[0].files[]
        | select(.filename | test("/crates/"))
        | {crate: (.filename | capture("/crates/(?<c>[^/]+)/").c), count: .summary.lines.count, covered: .summary.lines.covered}
        | [.crate, .count, .covered]
        | @tsv
      ' /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json \
      | awk -F'\t' -v threshold="{{threshold}}" '
          {sum[$1]+=$2; cov[$1]+=$3}
          END {
            for (c in sum) {
              pct = (cov[c]/sum[c]*100)
              status = (pct+0 < threshold+0) ? "FAIL" : "pass"
              printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%.2f\t%s\n", c, sum[c], cov[c], pct, status
            }
          }
        ' | sort)
    echo "$report" | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%-25s lines=%-6s covered=%-6s cover=%6s%%  %s\n", $1, $2, $3, $4, $5}'
    echo "$report" | grep -q FAIL && exit 1 || exit 0

# Clean build targets, Moon task caches, and generated artifacts
clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean
    rm -f lcov.info callisto-schema.json

# Fast pre-commit hook validation (<500ms formatting check)
pre-commit: fmt-check

# Pre-push hook validation: formatting check plus clippy on affected projects only
pre-push: fmt-check lint-affected

# Install native Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks
hooks:
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-commit' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-push' > .git/hooks/pre-push
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push
    @echo "Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks installed successfully."

# Static security audit of workflows and actions (requires zizmor and ripgrep).
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Credential-free release workflow contract, policy, and policy mutant checks.
release-workflow-checks:
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh --self-test

# Workflow Contracts CI job minus actionlint and zizmor: pins, release
# contract/policy, artifact build script, the Release-PR action contract
# under a minimal PATH, and the installer verification-mode tests.
workflow-contracts: release-workflow-checks
    bash .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-release-artifact-build-script.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-move-floating-tag.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_contract.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_download_extraction_format.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_action_ref_version_resolution.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_crates_io_fallback.sh

# Every check CI runs except actionlint (Docker) and the binary-dependent
# release-PR decide contract and artifact preflight build. CI runs them as
# parallel jobs (callisto-ci.yml); locally they run in sequence.
ci: fmt-check lint fuzz-check test audit doc-check zizmor workflow-contracts release-workflow-behavior (coverage "90")

        | {crate: (.filename | capture("/crates/(?<c>[^/]+)/").c), count: .summary.lines.count, covered: .summary.lines.covered}
        | [.crate, .count, .covered]
        | @tsv
      ' /tmp/callisto-cov-summary.json \
      | awk -F'\t' -v threshold="{{threshold}}" '
          {sum[$1]+=$2; cov[$1]+=$3}
          END {
            for (c in sum) {
              pct = (cov[c]/sum[c]*100)
              status = (pct+0 < threshold+0) ? "FAIL" : "pass"
              printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%.2f\t%s\n", c, sum[c], cov[c], pct, status
            }
          }
        ' | sort)
    echo "$report" | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%-25s lines=%-6s covered=%-6s cover=%6s%%  %s\n", $1, $2, $3, $4, $5}'
    echo "$report" | grep -q FAIL && exit 1 || exit 0

# Clean build targets, Moon task caches, and generated artifacts
clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean
    rm -f lcov.info callisto-schema.json

# Fast pre-commit hook validation (<500ms formatting check)
pre-commit: fmt-check

# Pre-push hook validation: formatting check plus clippy on affected projects only
pre-push: fmt-check lint-affected

# Install native Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks
hooks:
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-commit' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    @echo '#!/bin/sh\njust pre-push' > .git/hooks/pre-push
    @chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push
    @echo "Git pre-commit and pre-push hooks installed successfully."

# Static security audit of workflows and actions (requires zizmor and ripgrep).
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Credential-free release workflow contract, policy, and policy mutant checks.
release-workflow-checks:
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-contract.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh
    bash .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh --self-test

# Workflow Contracts CI job minus actionlint and zizmor: pins, release
# contract/policy, artifact build script, the Release-PR action contract
# under a minimal PATH, and the installer verification-mode tests.
workflow-contracts: release-workflow-checks
    bash .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-release-artifact-build-script.sh
    bash .github/tests/test-move-floating-tag.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_pr_contract.sh
    env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash .github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_release_contract.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_download_extraction_format.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_action_ref_version_resolution.sh
    bash .github/actions/setup-callisto/tests/test_crates_io_fallback.sh

# Every check CI runs except actionlint (Docker) and the binary-dependent
# release-PR decide contract and artifact preflight build. CI runs them as
# parallel jobs (callisto-ci.yml); locally they run in sequence.
ci: fmt-check lint fuzz-check test audit doc-check zizmor workflow-contracts release-workflow-behavior (coverage "90")

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged managed release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions: {}

# One group per commit: GitHub replaces a pending run in a shared group, which
# could silently drop a release merge queued behind an unrelated push.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 45
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Install registry test tools
        uses: $/.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Verify workflow contracts and reject mutable action references
        run: just workflow-contracts

  recovery-checks:
    name: Check release workflow policy for recovery
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_source_sha != ''
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install ripgrep
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: ripgrep
      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - name: Verify release workflow contracts
        run: just release-workflow-checks

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, recovery-checks]
    # Exactly one gate runs per event; a failed gate matches neither clause.
    if: >-
      always() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      ((needs.verify.result == 'success' && needs.recovery-checks.result == 'skipped') ||
       (needs.recovery-checks.result == 'success' && needs.verify.result == 'skipped'))
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
      orchestration_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Attestations are stamped with this run's own SHA, so the
          # coordinator must be exactly the revision running this workflow.
          orchestration_sha="$TRIGGERING_SHA"
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and .head.repo.full_name == "'"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"'" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            {
              echo 'is_release_pr=true'
              echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
              echo "orchestration_sha=$orchestration_sha"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: release-candidate
    if: >-
      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr != 'true' &&
      inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          # Interdependent Cargo packages bump together, so Cargo.lock must be refreshed in the release PR.
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    # always(): release-candidate's own ancestors include a gate that is skipped
    # by design, and a skipped ancestor silently skips any job without a status function.
    if: >-
      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      has_artifacts: ${{ steps.slots.outputs.has_artifacts }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The coordinator must be the current workflow revision. Recovery
          # never rebuilds its release engine from historic source.
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          mkdir -p "$handoff_dir"
          callisto release plan --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \
            --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \
            --decision "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source/.callisto/release-decision.json" \
            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          # Relative name: the consumers verify from a different runner OS and RUNNER_TEMP.
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256)
      - name: Read declared artifact slot count
        id: slots
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Own statement: set -e cannot see a substitution failing inside an echo argument.
          has_artifacts=$(jq '.artifactSlots | length > 0' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json")
          case "$has_artifacts" in
            true|false) ;;
            *) echo "::error::artifact slot probe returned '$has_artifacts'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "has_artifacts=$has_artifacts" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

  build-artifact:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} from the intent-bound source tree
    needs: [plan, release-candidate]
    if: always() && needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: macos-arm64
            runner: macos-14
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: macos-x64
            runner: macos-14
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-arm64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
            kind: cross
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Verify handoff
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts"
      - name: Build declared artifact
        env:
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/release-source
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
        run: |
          bash .github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh
      - name: Attest exact artifact bytes
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-build-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

  build:
    name: Assemble attested product artifacts
    needs: [build-artifact, release-candidate, plan]
    if: always() && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true' && needs.build-artifact.result == 'success'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    outputs:
      orchestration_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      # Every matrix target's artifact, so a target added to the matrix cannot be built and then left out of the manifest.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: release-build-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - name: Create exact artifact manifest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release artifact-manifest --intent "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json" --artifact-dir "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts" --out "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts/manifest.json"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: [plan, build, release-candidate]
    # Artifact-less sources skip build; a failed or cancelled build must still block.
    # !cancelled() not always(): a status function still defeats the skipped-ancestor
    # rule, but cancelling the run must stop the one irreversible job.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' &&
      (needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'false' || needs.build.result == 'success')
    timeout-minutes: 60
    concurrency:
      group: release-execute
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          # The release-source checkout alone needs Git credentials because
          # graph-owned tag dispatch pushes from this repository.
          persist-credentials: true
      # Downloaded outside the workspace (under $RUNNER_TEMP, like
      # setup-callisto's own binary install): callisto release execute
      # re-checks release trust before every dispatch, which requires a
      # worktree with no tracked or untracked files -- landing these inside
      # the checkout would dirty it and fail that check before anything
      # gets published.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        env:
          HAS_ARTIFACTS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          (cd "$intent_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          if [[ "$HAS_ARTIFACTS" == true ]]; then
            cmp "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" "$build_dir/release-intent/release-intent.json"
          fi
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          receipt_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$receipt_dir"
          args=(--source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" --intent "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" --receipt "$receipt_dir/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA")
          if [[ -f "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" --artifact-dir "$build_dir/release-artifacts")
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
      # Needs no secrets: a plain tag push with the checkout's Git credentials, like the release tags. A no-op before 1.0.0.
      - name: Move the floating major tag
        working-directory: release-source
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
        run: bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/move-floating-tag.sh" .callisto/release-decision.json cargo/callisto-cli "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA"
      - name: Summarize receipt
        if: always()
        run: |
          receipt="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/release-receipt.json"
          if [[ -f "$receipt" ]]; then
            {
              echo '### Release receipt'
              echo '```json'
              cat "$receipt"
              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
      - name: Upload receipt
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          # Per attempt: keeps each attempt's receipt instead of shadowing the prior one.
          name: release-receipt-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/callisto-release-receipt/${{ github.run_id }}
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

1	use std::path::PathBuf;

3	use clap::{Args, Parser, Subcommand, ValueEnum};
4	
5	/// Changesets-style version and release manager for Cargo, npm and Python workspaces.
6	#[derive(Parser)]
7	#[command(name = "callisto", version, disable_help_subcommand = true)]
8	pub struct Cli {
9	    #[command(flatten)]
10	    pub global: GlobalArgs,
11	    #[command(subcommand)]
12	    pub command: Command,
13	}
14	
15	/// Flags shared by every subcommand.
16	#[derive(Args, Clone, Debug)]
17	pub struct GlobalArgs {
18	    /// Output format for command results.
19	    #[arg(long, global = true, value_enum, default_value = "text")]
20	    pub format: OutputFormat,
21	
22	    /// Workspace directory to operate in (defaults to the current directory).
23	    #[arg(long, global = true, default_value = ".")]
24	    pub cwd: PathBuf,
25	
26	    #[arg(
27	        long,
28	        global = true,
29	        help = "Preview manifest and file changes without writing to disk"
30	    )]
31	    pub dry_run: bool,
32	}
33	
34	/// Output rendering mode: human-readable text or machine-readable JSON.
35	#[derive(ValueEnum, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
36	pub enum OutputFormat {
37	    Text,
38	    Json,
39	}
40	
41	/// A callisto subcommand.
42	#[derive(Subcommand, Clone, Debug)]
43	pub enum Command {
44	    /// Create a new changeset describing pending package changes.
45	    Add(AddArgs),
46	    /// Show the workspace's pending changesets and diagnostics.
47	    Status(StatusArgs),
48	    /// Print the workspace's native-build target matrix as JSON or a table.
49	    #[command(hide = true)]
50	    Matrix(MatrixArgs),
51	    /// Consume pending changesets and bump package versions accordingly.
52	    Version(VersionArgs),
53	    /// Manage prerelease mode for the workspace.
54	    #[command(subcommand)]
55	    Pre(PreArgs),
56	    /// Apply a temporary, non-persistent version bump for a snapshot release.
57	    Snapshot(SnapshotArgs),
58	    /// Scaffold Callisto configuration in the current workspace.
59	    Init(InitArgs),
60	    /// Generate a pull request body summarizing pending release changes.
61	    #[command(hide = true)]
62	    ComposePrBody(ComposePrBodyArgs),
63	    /// Publish every package whose current version has not been released yet.
64	    Release(ReleaseCommandArgs),
65	    /// Decide the next managed release-pull-request operation from a forge snapshot.
66	    #[command(subcommand, hide = true)]
67	    ReleasePr(ReleasePrArgs),
68	    /// Generate shell completion scripts.
69	    Completions(CompletionsArgs),
70	    /// Print the JSON schema for a report type.
71	    #[command(hide = true)]
72	    Schema(SchemaArgs),
73	    /// Print a subcommand's help text.
74	    #[command(hide = true)]
75	    Help(HelpArgs),
76	}
77	
78	impl Command {
79	    /// This subcommand's name exactly as clap parses it, for the JSON error
80	    /// envelope's `"command"` field -- computed from the parsed subcommand
81	    /// rather than duplicated as a literal at each error call site.
82	    pub fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
83	        match self {
84	            Command::Add(_) => "add",
85	            Command::Status(_) => "status",
86	            Command::Matrix(_) => "matrix",
87	            Command::Version(_) => "version",
88	            Command::Pre(_) => "pre",
89	            Command::Snapshot(_) => "snapshot",
90	            Command::Init(_) => "init",
91	            Command::ComposePrBody(_) => "compose-pr-body",
92	            Command::Release(_) => "release",
93	            Command::ReleasePr(_) => "release-pr",
94	            Command::Completions(_) => "completions",
95	            Command::Schema(_) => "schema",
96	            Command::Help(_) => "help",
97	        }
98	    }
99	}
100	
101	/// Arguments for the `schema` command.
102	#[derive(Args, Clone, Debug, Default)]
103	pub struct SchemaArgs {
104	    /// Report type to print the schema for; defaults to status.
105	    #[arg(long = "type", value_enum)]
106	    pub target_type: Option<SchemaReportType>,
107	}
108	
109	/// The one registry of report/document types `schema --type` can print --

8	/// ```json

21	/// `command` is the subcommand that was parsed before the error occurred
22	/// (see [`crate::cli::Command::name`]), not derived from the error itself --
23	/// an error can occur before enough context exists to reconstruct it any
24	/// other way (e.g. an argument-parsing failure).
25	///
26	/// `"code"`, `"message"`, `"help"`, and `"path"` are always present;

29	/// serialized.

36	        "command": command,

38	            "code": code,

use callisto_graph::locate::LocateError;
use callisto_graph::{ConfigError, GraphError};
use callisto_model::CommandError;
use miette::Diagnostic;

/// Formats a [`CliError`] as a JSON value with a consistent error envelope:
///
/// ```json
/// {
///   "schemaVersion": 1,
///   "command": "add",
///   "error": {
///     "code": "E211",
///     "message": "human-readable error text",
///     "help": "optional guidance string or null",
///     "path": "optional filesystem path or null"
///   }
/// }
/// ```
///
/// `command` is the subcommand that was parsed before the error occurred
/// (see [`crate::cli::Command::name`]), not derived from the error itself --
/// an error can occur before enough context exists to reconstruct it any
/// other way (e.g. an argument-parsing failure).
///
/// `"code"`, `"message"`, `"help"`, and `"path"` are always present;
/// `"help"`/`"path"` are `null` when the diagnostic provides none. This
/// guarantees a stable shape regardless of which [`CliError`] variant is
/// serialized.
pub fn format_error_json(command: &str, err: &CliError) -> serde_json::Value {
    let code = err.code().map(|c| c.to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|| "E000".to_string());
    let help = err.help().map(|h| h.to_string());
    let path = err.path().map(|p| p.display().to_string());
    serde_json::json!({
        "schemaVersion": callisto_model::SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "command": command,
        "error": {
            "code": code,
            "message": err.to_string(),
            "help": help,
            "path": path,
        }
    })
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error, Diagnostic)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum CliError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Graph(#[from] GraphError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Locate(#[from] LocateError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Config(#[from] ConfigError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Command(#[from] CommandError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E211),
        help("verify registry credentials/authentication and network connectivity, then retry")
    )]
    Registry(#[from] callisto_model::RegistryError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    ChangesetParse(#[from] callisto_model::format::ParseError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    ChangesetWrite(#[from] callisto_model::format::WriteError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Manifest(#[from] callisto_model::ManifestError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Vcs(#[from] callisto_model::vcs::VcsError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    ReleasePrDecision(#[from] callisto_model::ReleasePrDecisionError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    ReleaseIntent(#[from] callisto_model::ReleaseIntentError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Model(#[from] callisto_model::ModelError),

    #[error("interactive prompt failed: {0}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E269),
        help("pass flags explicitly to skip interactive prompts, or run in a terminal")
    )]
    Interactive(#[from] dialoguer::Error),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E212),
        help("Check that .changeset/pre.json is valid JSON and was not partially written.")
    )]
    PreJson(#[from] callisto_model::format::PreJsonError),

    #[error("I/O error{}", match &path {
        Some(p) => format!(" accessing `{}`", p.display()),
        None => String::new(),
    })]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E213),
        help("check that the path exists and that you have permission to access it")
    )]
    Io {
        #[source]
        source: std::io::Error,
        path: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    },

    #[error("refusing to prompt interactively: stdin is not a terminal; missing: --package")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E214),
        help("specify package names explicitly via `callisto add --package <name>:<severity>` in CI environments")
    )]
    NotATty,

    #[error("release intent `{}` declares schema version {found}, but this build reads version {expected}", path.display())]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E215),
        help("re-run `callisto release plan` to derive a fresh intent: an intent is bound to one build's operation graph and is never reused across versions")
    )]
    ReleaseIntentSchemaUnsupported {
        path: std::path::PathBuf,
        found: String,
        expected: u8,
    },

    #[error("release artifact-manifest needs an output file; remove --dry-run because it records build output")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E216), help("re-run `callisto release artifact-manifest` without --dry-run"))]
    ReleaseArtifactManifestDryRun,

    #[error("release plan needs an output file; remove --dry-run because planning is already read-only")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E217), help("re-run `callisto release plan --out <file>` without --dry-run"))]
    ReleasePlanDryRun,

    #[error("release execute cannot run with --dry-run")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E218), help("remove --dry-run; release execute has no read-only mode"))]
    ReleaseExecuteDryRun,

    #[error("release intent declares no binary artifact slots; no artifact manifest can be created")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E219), help("plan the release with --orchestration-revision and --artifact-repository so the intent declares artifact slots"))]
    ReleaseNoArtifactSlots,

    #[error("release intent publishes no Python package; there is nothing to build or seal")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E308),
        help("drop --seal-python and `release build-python` for an intent without a Python publish")
    )]
    ReleaseNoPythonPublishes,

    #[error("release build-python writes build output; remove --dry-run")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E309), help("re-run `callisto release build-python` without --dry-run"))]
    ReleaseBuildPythonDryRun,

    #[error("artifact manifests require a Git commit release source")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E220), help("plan the release from a Git commit source"))]
    ReleaseManifestSourceNotGit,

    #[error("artifact `{asset}` must be a regular file directly in `{dir}`")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E221),
        help("place the built asset as a plain file (not a symlink or directory) directly in the artifact directory")
    )]
    ReleaseArtifactNotRegularFile { asset: String, dir: String },

    #[error("artifact `{asset}` resolves outside `{dir}`")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E222),
        help("remove symlinks so every asset resolves inside the artifact directory")
    )]
    ReleaseArtifactEscapesDirectory { asset: String, dir: String },

    #[error("cannot create artifact manifest: {detail}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E223),
        help("check that the artifact directory holds exactly the assets the intent declares")
    )]
    ReleaseManifestInvalid { detail: String },

    #[error("invalid merged release commit `{raw}`: {detail}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E224), help("pass the full commit SHA of the merged release commit"))]
    ReleaseCommitInvalid { raw: String, detail: String },

    #[error("release decision {decision} must be inside selected source root {root}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E225),
        help("point --decision at a file inside the source root selected with --source-root")
    )]
    ReleaseDecisionOutsideSource { decision: String, root: String },

    #[error("invalid release decision path {path}: {detail}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E226), help("pass a repository-relative decision path without `..` components"))]
    ReleaseDecisionPathInvalid { path: String, detail: String },

    #[error("invalid release package `{raw}`: {detail}; use an exact ecosystem-qualified identity such as cargo/callisto-cli")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E227),
        help("name each package as <ecosystem>/<name>, for example cargo/callisto-cli")
    )]
    ReleasePackageInvalid { raw: String, detail: String },

    #[error("invalid orchestration revision `{revision}`: {detail}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E228), help("pass the full commit SHA of the orchestration workflow revision"))]
    ReleaseOrchestrationRevisionInvalid { revision: String, detail: String },

    #[error("invalid artifact repository `{repository}`: {detail}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E229), help("pass the forge repository as <owner>/<repo>"))]
    ReleaseArtifactRepositoryInvalid { repository: String, detail: String },

    #[error("[release].forge-repository is `{configured}`, but the release targets `{requested}`")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E230),
        help("plan with an --artifact-repository matching [release].forge-repository in callisto.toml")
    )]
    ReleaseForgeRepositoryMismatch { configured: String, requested: String },

    #[error("product release planning requires --orchestration-revision and --artifact-repository")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E231), help("pass both --orchestration-revision and --artifact-repository"))]
    ReleaseOrchestrationFlagsRequired,

    #[error("release intent declares no binary artifact slots and the manifest seals no Python files; omit --artifact-manifest and --artifact-dir")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E232),
        help(
            "drop --artifact-manifest and --artifact-dir for an intent without artifact slots or sealed Python files"
        )
    )]
    ReleaseUnexpectedArtifactInputs,

    #[error("release intent declares binary artifact slots; provide both --artifact-manifest and --artifact-dir")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E233), help("pass both --artifact-manifest and --artifact-dir"))]
    ReleaseMissingArtifactInputs,

    #[error("release run envelope is not valid for this intent: {detail}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E234),
        help("re-check the orchestration revision and artifact manifest against the intent")
    )]
    ReleaseEnvelopeInvalid { detail: String },

    #[error("cannot issue terminal release receipt: {detail}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E235),
        help("re-run `callisto release execute`; it adopts effects that already landed")
    )]
    ReleaseReceiptIssue { detail: String },

    #[error("invalid release intent {path}: {detail}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E236), help("re-run `callisto release plan` to derive a fresh intent"))]
    ReleaseIntentInvalid { path: String, detail: String },

    #[error("invalid artifact manifest {path}: {detail}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E237), help("re-run `callisto release artifact-manifest` to regenerate it"))]
    ArtifactManifestFileInvalid { path: String, detail: String },

    #[error("invalid JSON in {path}: {detail}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E238), help("check the file is complete, well-formed JSON"))]
    ReleaseJsonInvalid { path: String, detail: String },

    #[error("this workspace cannot release locally: {reason}")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E239),
        help("release it from CI with `callisto release plan`, `callisto release artifact-manifest`, then `callisto release execute`; `callisto release --dry-run` still previews it locally")
    )]
    ReleaseRequiresCiRoute { reason: String },

    #[error("stdin is not a terminal, so init needs flags instead of prompts; missing: {}", .missing.join(", "))]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E240),
        help("re-run `callisto init --yes` with the listed flags, or run it in a terminal to be asked")
    )]
    InitRequiresYes { missing: Vec<&'static str> },

    #[error("init --yes is missing required flag(s): {}", .missing.join(", "))]
    #[diagnostic(code(E241), help("supply the listed flags; see `callisto init --help`"))]
    InitMissingFlags { missing: Vec<&'static str> },

    #[error("--workflow and --no-workflow are mutually exclusive")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E242), help("pass only one of --workflow or --no-workflow"))]
    InitWorkflowFlagsConflict,

    #[error("`--{flag}` only applies with --artifact-target")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E298),
        help("drop --{flag}, or pass --artifact-target to ship the product's binaries")
    )]
    InitFlagRequiresArtifactTarget { flag: &'static str },

    #[error("`--{flag}` requires an `origin` remote, and none is configured")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E299),
        help("add the repository's remote as `origin` (`git remote add origin <url>`), then re-run init")
    )]
    InitFlagRequiresOrigin { flag: &'static str },

    #[error("workspace is already in pre-release mode")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E243),
        help("run `callisto pre exit` first, or delete .changeset/pre.json manually to reset")
    )]
    PreAlreadyActive,

    #[error("workspace is not in pre-release mode")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E244), help("callisto pre enter <tag>"))]
    PreNotActive,

    #[error("release pull requests do not support pre-release mode (tag `{tag}`)")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(E318),
        help("release prereleases locally with `callisto version` and `callisto release`, or run `callisto pre exit` first")
    )]
    ReleasePrInPreMode { tag: String },

    #[error("frontmatter opened with `---` on line 1 but was never closed with a matching `---`")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E041), help("Ensure frontmatter block closes with `---`."))]
    UnclosedFrontmatter,

    #[error("line {line}: quoted name is never closed with a matching `\"`")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E042))]
    UnclosedQuotedName { line: usize },

    #[error("line {line}: quoted name `{raw}` is followed by unexpected content before the `:` separator")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E043))]
    AmbiguousNameQuoting { line: usize, raw: String },

    #[error("line {line}: no `:` separator found in {raw:?}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E044))]
    MissingSeparator { line: usize, raw: String },

    #[error("line {line}: package name is empty")]
    #[diagnostic(code(E045))]
    EmptyName { line: usize },

    #[diagnostic(code(E046))]
    InvalidSeverity {

1	//! Pure argv construction for "publish a package to its registry", plus
2	//! subprocess-output classification for the same three ecosystems (Cargo,
3	//! npm, PyPI).
4	//!
5	//! This module owns exactly two questions per ecosystem: *what command do we
6	//! run* (given package/plan facts and already-detected environment facts --
7	//! never a [`callisto_model::CommandRunner`] call of its own) and *what did
8	//! the finished command's output mean*. Actually invoking the command, and
9	//! any retry/backoff policy around a failed attempt, is the caller's job --
10	//! see the durable release executor's single production publish path.
11	//!
12	//! A small amount of local filesystem reading happens here (the Cargo
13	//! on-disk version check, npm package-manager detection from lockfiles, the
14	//! PyPI interpreter's PATH lookup) -- that's "gathering the facts needed to
15	//! build the right argv", not executing a publish. It never shells out.
16	
17	use std::ffi::OsStr;
18	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
19	use std::time::Duration;
20	
21	use callisto_manifests::WorkspaceCargoResolver;
22	use callisto_model::{CommandOutput, Ecosystem, NpmAccess, PackageId, PublishOutcome, RegistryError, Version};
23	
24	use crate::error::{GraphError, ReleasePreconditionRequirement};
25	
26	/// Default fallback wait (seconds) when a registry does not supply a
27	/// `retry_after` value and the classifier cannot parse one from output.
28	const DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_SECS: u64 = 60;
29	
30	/// One subprocess invocation: program, args, and working directory. Building
31	/// this is the entire job of the `*_publish_argv` functions below --
32	/// executing it is the caller's.
33	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
34	pub struct Argv {
35	    pub program: String,
36	    pub args: Vec<String>,
37	    pub cwd: PathBuf,
38	}
39	
40	// ---------------------------------------------------------------- cargo
41	
42	/// Builds the exact `cargo publish` argv for one crate: `--manifest-path`
43	/// (so the caller can keep the workspace root as its own working directory)
44	/// plus `--locked`, so a stale `Cargo.lock` fails the publish immediately
45	/// instead of `cargo` silently re-resolving one at publish time.
46	/// `registry_key` is `Some` only for a non-default registry -- crates.io is
47	/// the implicit default and never needs `--registry`.
48	///
49	/// Before returning, verifies that the on-disk `Cargo.toml` version under
50	/// `package_dir` (resolving `version.workspace = true` against the
51	/// workspace root's `[workspace.package].version` when present) matches
52	/// `version` -- this is the one behavior `SubprocessRegistryClient` had that
53	/// the durable release executor's own `dispatch_registry` had silently
54	/// dropped: it catches the common mistake of running `release execute`
55	/// without first running `callisto version`, which would otherwise silently
56	/// publish the old on-disk version.
57	pub fn cargo_publish_argv(
58	    workspace_root: &Path,
59	    package_dir: &Path,
60	    package_name: &str,
61	    version: &Version,
62	    registry_key: Option<&str>,
63	) -> Result<Argv, GraphError> {
64	    verify_cargo_ondisk_version(workspace_root, package_dir, package_name, version)?;
65	
66	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
67	    let mut args = vec![
68	        "publish".to_string(),
69	        "--manifest-path".to_string(),
70	        manifest_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
71	        "--locked".to_string(),
72	    ];
73	    if let Some(reg) = registry_key {
74	        args.push("--registry".to_string());
75	        args.push(reg.to_string());
76	    }
77	    Ok(Argv {
78	        program: "cargo".to_string(),
79	        args,
80	        cwd: cargo_workspace_dir(workspace_root, package_dir)?,
81	    })
82	}
83	
84	/// The directory of the Cargo workspace the package at `package_dir` belongs to. Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml`
85	/// (registries, credentials) from where it runs, so a command about the package runs here, not at the workspace root.
86	pub(crate) fn cargo_workspace_dir(workspace_root: &Path, package_dir: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, GraphError> {
87	    let root_manifest = callisto_manifests::cargo_workspace_of(
88	        &mut callisto_manifests::WorkspaceReads::default(),
89	        workspace_root,
90	        &package_dir.join("Cargo.toml"),
91	    )?;
92	    Ok(workspace_root.join(root_manifest.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(""))))
93	}
94	
95	fn verify_cargo_ondisk_version(
96	    workspace_root: &Path,
97	    package_dir: &Path,
98	    package_name: &str,
99	    planned: &Version,
100	) -> Result<(), GraphError> {
101	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
102	    let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&manifest_path).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
103	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
104	        message: error.to_string(),
105	    })?;
106	    // Parse only the [package].version field -- no need for full CST. A
107	    // permissive `toml::Value` intermediate rather than a direct `String`
108	    // deserialization, because `version.workspace = true` (Cargo's
109	    // workspace-version-inheritance syntax) parses `version` as a table, not
110	    // a string.
111	    let parsed = toml::from_str::<toml::Value>(&contents).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
112	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
113	        message: error.to_string(),
114	    })?;
115	    let version_value =
116	        parsed
117	            .get("package")
118	            .and_then(|p| p.get("version"))
119	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
120	                path: manifest_path.clone(),
121	                message: "missing [package].version".to_string(),
122	            })?;
123	
124	    let on_disk = if let Some(s) = version_value.as_str() {
125	        s.to_string()
126	    } else if version_value.get("workspace").and_then(toml::Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
127	        let member = package_dir.join("Cargo.toml");
128	        let document = callisto_manifests::parse_manifest(&member, &contents)?;
129	        let root_manifest = callisto_manifests::enclosing_workspace_manifest(workspace_root, &member, &document)?
130	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
131	                path: manifest_path.clone(),
132	                message: "`version.workspace = true` but no Cargo workspace governs it".to_string(),
133	            })?;
134	        let root_manifest_path = workspace_root.join(&root_manifest);
135	        let resolver = WorkspaceCargoResolver::load_at(workspace_root, &root_manifest)?;
136	        let ws_version = resolver
137	            .workspace_version()?
138	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
139	                path: root_manifest_path.clone(),
140	                message: "`version.workspace = true` but the workspace root has no [workspace.package].version"
141	                    .to_string(),
142	            })?;
143	        ws_version.render().to_string()
144	    } else {
145	        return Err(GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
146	            path: manifest_path,
147	            message: "[package].version is neither a string nor a `{ workspace = true }` table".to_string(),
148	        });
149	    };
150	
151	    let found = Version::parse(&on_disk, planned.grammar())?;
152	    if found != *planned {
153	        return Err(GraphError::OnDiskVersionDrift {
154	            package: PackageId::Prefixed {
155	                ecosystem: Ecosystem::Cargo,
156	                name: package_name.to_string(),
157	            },
158	            expected: planned.clone(),
159	            found,
160	        });
161	    }
162	    Ok(())
163	}
164	
165	// ------------------------------------------------------------------ npm
166	
167	/// The npm-compatible package manager a workspace uses, detected from
168	/// lockfile presence. Each one needs a materially different invocation to
169	/// publish a single named package out of a monorepo -- see
170	/// [`npm_publish_argv`].
171	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
172	pub enum NpmPackageManager {
173	    Pnpm,
174	    Yarn,
175	    Bun,
176	    Npm,
177	}
178	
179	/// Detects the npm-compatible package manager of the workspace in `workspace_dir` from the files that mark it.
180	/// Detection priority: pnpm > yarn > bun > npm (default). A `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is pnpm even where the lockfile is not
181	/// committed, and a file that cannot be inspected is an error, not a reason to fall back to `npm`.
182	///
183	/// This is real, live-today correctness content: the durable release
184	/// executor's `dispatch_registry` used to hardcode plain `npm publish`
185	/// regardless of which package manager a workspace actually uses, so a pnpm
186	/// or yarn workspace published with the wrong tool.
187	///
188	/// # Errors
189	///
190	/// A marker file cannot be inspected.
191	pub fn detect_npm_package_manager(workspace_dir: &Path) -> Result<NpmPackageManager, GraphError> {
192	    let present = |name: &str| -> Result<bool, GraphError> {
193	        let path = workspace_dir.join(name);
194	        callisto_model::strict_fs::exists(&path).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
195	            path,
196	            message: error.to_string(),
197	        })
198	    };
199	    Ok(if present("pnpm-lock.yaml")? || present("pnpm-workspace.yaml")? {
200	        NpmPackageManager::Pnpm
201	    } else if present("yarn.lock")? {
202	        NpmPackageManager::Yarn
203	    } else if present("bun.lockb")? || present("bun.lock")? {
204	        // bun.lockb is the legacy binary lockfile format; bun.lock (text) is
205	        // written by Bun >= 1.1.1. Both signal a bun-managed workspace.
206	        NpmPackageManager::Bun
207	    } else {
208	        NpmPackageManager::Npm
209	    })
210	}
211	
212	/// Builds the npm-ecosystem publish argv for one package, given the
213	/// already-detected `package_manager` (see [`detect_npm_package_manager`]).
214	///
215	/// | Package manager | Program | Base args                                  |
216	/// |------------------|---------|--------------------------------------------|
217	/// | Pnpm             | `pnpm`  | `publish --filter=<name> --no-git-checks`  |
218	/// | Yarn             | `yarn`  | `workspace <name> npm publish`             |
219	/// | Bun              | `bun`   | `publish` (run from `package_dir`)         |
220	/// | Npm              | `npm`   | `publish --workspace=<name>`               |
221	///
222	/// `--filter=`/`--workspace=` use the joined form so the name cannot be
223	/// re-read as an option. Yarn takes the name positionally and has no joined
224	/// spelling, so there it rests on `ReleasePackageId`'s leading-`-` rejection.
225	///
226	/// `tag`/`access`/`registry` are appended to every variant's base args.
227	/// `package_dir` is only used for bun: it has no `--filter`/`--workspace`
228	/// flag to target one package by name, so it alone must run from the
229	/// package's own directory rather than the workspace root.
230	pub fn npm_publish_argv(
231	    workspace_root: &Path,
232	    package_dir: &Path,
233	    package_name: &str,
234	    package_manager: NpmPackageManager,
235	    tag: Option<&str>,
236	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
237	    registry: Option<&str>,
238	) -> Argv {
239	    let extra = npm_publish_flags(package_name, tag, access, registry);
240	
241	    let (program, mut args, cwd) = match package_manager {
242	        NpmPackageManager::Pnpm => (
243	            "pnpm",
244	            vec![
245	                "publish".to_string(),
246	                // `--filter=<name>`, not `--filter <name>`: the joined form
247	                // cannot be re-read as an option even if a name slipped past
248	                // `ReleasePackageId`'s charset rule.
249	                format!("--filter={package_name}"),
250	                // pnpm >= 7 refuses to publish from a dirty working tree by
251	                // default. After `callisto version` stages manifest bumps,
252	                // the tree is always dirty until the operator commits, so
253	                // this bypasses the git-status check.
254	                "--no-git-checks".to_string(),
255	            ],
256	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
257	        ),
258	        NpmPackageManager::Yarn => (
259	            "yarn",
260	            vec![
261	                "workspace".to_string(),
262	                package_name.to_string(),
263	                "npm".to_string(),
264	                "publish".to_string(),
265	            ],
266	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
267	        ),
268	        NpmPackageManager::Bun => ("bun", vec!["publish".to_string()], workspace_root.join(package_dir)),
269	        NpmPackageManager::Npm => (
270	            "npm",
271	            vec!["publish".to_string(), format!("--workspace={package_name}")],
272	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
273	        ),
274	    };
275	    args.extend(extra);
276	    Argv {
277	        program: program.to_string(),
278	        args,
279	        cwd,
280	    }
281	}
282	
283	/// The access an npm package publishes with: the explicit `publishConfig.access`,
284	/// else `public` for a scoped `@scope/name` (npm defaults scoped packages to restricted).
285	pub fn npm_default_access(name: &str, explicit: Option<NpmAccess>) -> Option<NpmAccess> {
286	    explicit.or_else(|| name.starts_with('@').then_some(NpmAccess::Public))
287	}
288	
289	/// `--tag`/`--access`/`--registry`, shared by every npm-ecosystem publish argv.
290	fn npm_publish_flags(
291	    package_name: &str,
292	    tag: Option<&str>,
293	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
294	    registry: Option<&str>,
295	) -> Vec<String> {
296	    let mut extra: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
297	    if let Some(t) = tag {
298	        extra.push("--tag".to_string());
299	        extra.push(t.to_string());
300	    }
301	    if let Some(access) = npm_default_access(package_name, access) {
302	        extra.push("--access".to_string());
303	        extra.push(
304	            match access {
305	                NpmAccess::Public => "public",
306	                NpmAccess::Restricted => "restricted",
307	            }
308	            .to_string(),
309	        );
310	    }
311	    if let Some(reg) = registry {
312	        extra.push("--registry".to_string());
313	        extra.push(reg.to_string());
314	    }
315	    extra
316	}
317	
318	/// Publishes the package in `package_dir` by path: `npm publish <dir>` from `workspace_dir` (the workspace that owns
319	/// it, where its `.npmrc` is read), whatever the package manager. pnpm `--filter`, yarn
320	/// `workspace`, and npm `--workspace` select only workspace members, and an npm
321	/// platform package directory usually is not one. The path is absolute, so it
322	/// cannot be read as an option.
323	pub fn npm_publish_directory_argv(
324	    workspace_root: &Path,
325	    workspace_dir: &Path,
326	    package_dir: &Path,
327	    package_name: &str,
328	    tag: Option<&str>,
329	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
330	    registry: Option<&str>,
331	) -> Argv {
332	    let mut args = vec![
333	        "publish".to_string(),
334	        workspace_root.join(package_dir).to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
335	    ];
336	    args.extend(npm_publish_flags(package_name, tag, access, registry));
337	    Argv {
338	        program: "npm".to_string(),
339	        args,
340	        cwd: workspace_root.join(workspace_dir),
341	    }
342	}
343	
344	// ----------------------------------------------------------------- pypi
345	
346	/// `python -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir <outdir>` in the package directory, with the first interpreter on PATH
347	/// and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` set so backends that honor it stamp the same time into every rebuild.
348	pub fn pypi_build_argv(
349	    workspace_root: &Path,
350	    package_dir: &Path,
351	    outdir: &Path,
352	    source_date_epoch: u64,
353	) -> Result<Argv, GraphError> {
354	    let interpreter = resolve_python_interpreter(std::env::var_os("PATH").as_deref())?;
355	    Ok(Argv {
356	        program: "env".to_string(),
357	        args: vec![
358	            format!("SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH={source_date_epoch}"),
359	            interpreter.to_string(),
360	            "-m".to_string(),
361	            "build".to_string(),
362	            "--sdist".to_string(),
363	            "--wheel".to_string(),
364	            "--outdir".to_string(),
365	            outdir.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
366	        ],
367	        cwd: workspace_root.join(package_dir),
368	    })
369	}
370	
371	/// `twine upload` of exactly `files`, never a glob or `--skip-existing`, which skips by name without comparing bytes.
372	pub fn pypi_upload_argv(workspace_root: &Path, package_dir: &Path, index: Option<&str>, files: &[PathBuf]) -> Argv {
373	    let mut args = vec!["upload".to_string()];
374	    if let Some(index) = index {
375	        args.push("--repository-url".to_string());
376	        args.push(index.to_string());
377	    }
378	    args.extend(files.iter().map(|file| file.to_string_lossy().into_owned()));
379	    Argv {
380	        program: "twine".to_string(),
381	        args,
382	        cwd: workspace_root.join(package_dir),
383	    }
384	}
385	
386	/// Resolves the interpreter for the PyPI build step's `python -m build`:
387	/// prefers `python3` -- the only name macOS and Debian systems guarantee --
388	/// and falls back to bare `python` for systems that only ship that. Errors
389	/// naming both when neither is on `path_value`.
390	///
391	/// `path_value` is injected rather than read from `$PATH` directly so tests
392	/// can exercise both resolutions and the error without mutating process-wide
393	/// environment state.
394	fn resolve_python_interpreter(path_value: Option<&OsStr>) -> Result<&'static str, GraphError> {
395	    if exists_on_path("python3", path_value) {
396	        Ok("python3")
397	    } else if exists_on_path("python", path_value) {
398	        Ok("python")
399	    } else {
400	        Err(GraphError::ReleasePreconditionUnmet {
401	            requirement: ReleasePreconditionRequirement::PythonInterpreterOnPath,
402	        })
403	    }
404	}
405	
406	/// Whether `program` exists as a file in some directory of `path_value` --
407	/// PATH-lookup semantics, without ever spawning it.
408	fn exists_on_path(program: &str, path_value: Option<&OsStr>) -> bool {
409	    path_value.is_some_and(|path| std::env::split_paths(path).any(|dir| dir.join(program).is_file()))
410	}
411	
412	// ---- shared output-classification helpers --------------------------------
413	
414	fn combined_lower(output: &CommandOutput) -> String {
415	    format!("{}\n{}", output.stdout, output.stderr).to_lowercase()
416	}
417	
418	/// What a failed publish said: the last lines of redacted stdout, then redacted stderr. pnpm and twine print their
419	/// errors to stdout, so stderr alone can leave the failure message empty.
420	fn failure_detail(output: &CommandOutput) -> String {
421	    const STDOUT_TAIL_LINES: usize = 8;
422	    let stdout = callisto_model::redact_command_stderr(&output.stdout);
423	    let tail: Vec<&str> = stdout.lines().rev().take(STDOUT_TAIL_LINES).collect();
424	    let tail = tail.into_iter().rev().collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
425	    let stderr = output.redacted_stderr();
426	    [tail.trim(), stderr.trim()]
427	        .into_iter()
428	        .filter(|part| !part.is_empty())
429	        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
430	        .join("\n")
431	}
432	
433	/// Parses a numeric retry-after value (seconds) as reported by a registry
434	/// tool's output.
435	fn parse_retry_after(raw: &str) -> Option<Duration> {
436	    raw.trim().parse::<u64>().ok().map(Duration::from_secs)
437	}
438	
439	/// Looks for a `retry after <N>` mention in already-lowercased text and
440	/// parses `<N>` as a whole-second duration.

name: 'Setup Callisto Environment'
description: 'Sets up Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, moon and the .prototools toolchain, and Callisto CLI'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto installs the requested release version; local builds validated Callisto checkout source and ignores version. Release jobs must use local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: >-
      Version tag of Callisto to install. Default 'latest' installs the release this action's
      own invocation is pinned to (github.action_ref resolved against callisto@ tags), falling
      back to the newest published release when that ref is unset or unresolvable.
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  verification:
    description: >-
      Attestation verification of the prebuilt release asset (gh attestation verify, repo
      orin-dx/callisto, signer workflow callisto-release.yml). One of: require = a failed
      verification or missing gh aborts the step and the asset is never run; fallback (default) =
      on failure or missing gh, warn, delete the asset and install from crates.io instead (never
      run the unverified asset); skip = do not verify, warn, and use the asset. Releases built
      before the first attested release carry no attestation, hence the fallback default.
    required: false
    default: 'fallback'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt
        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"

    - name: Install moon and the .prototools toolchain
      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
      with:
        auto-install: true

    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION: ${{ inputs.verification }}
        GITHUB_ACTION_REF: ${{ github.action_ref }}
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      run: bash "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/scripts/install-callisto.sh" # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not action input or downloaded archive content.
name: 'Install registry test tools'
description: 'Installs the local npm, PyPI and Cargo registries the real-registry e2e tests run against. Linux only; the tests fail without them under CI.'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Verdaccio (real-registry npm e2e coverage)
      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
      shell: bash
      run: npm install -g verdaccio@6.10.4 # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] pinned to an exact upstream release; a CI-only test-registry tool, not a shipped or lockfile-tracked dependency.
    - name: Install pypiserver (real-registry PyPI e2e coverage)
      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
      shell: bash
      # legacy-cgi: pypiserver 2.4.0 imports `cgi`, removed in Python 3.13.
      # gunicorn: the test's `--server gunicorn` avoids a slow getfqdn() bind.
      # setuptools/wheel: the test builds with `--no-isolation` against this venv's build
      # backend, so no network fetch happens during `python -m build`; must be pre-installed.
      run: | # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not attacker-controlled input.
        python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv"
        "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv/bin/pip" install pypiserver==2.4.0 twine==6.2.0 build==1.4.4 legacy-cgi==2.6.3 gunicorn==26.2.0 setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1
        echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
    - name: Install cargo-http-registry (real-registry Cargo e2e coverage)
      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
      shell: bash
      run: cargo install --locked cargo-http-registry@0.1.8 # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] pinned to an exact upstream release; a CI-only test-registry tool, not a shipped or lockfile-tracked dependency.
