name: 'Callisto Validate Action'
description: 'Validates pending changesets, package discovery, configuration health, and release plan DAG'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Setup Callisto Environment
      uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto

    - name: Validate Configuration, Package Discovery & Changesets
      shell: bash
      env:
        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
      # `callisto status --check` is a conventional
      # 0/1 gate: 0 when there are no error-level diagnostics, 1 otherwise,
      # regardless of pending changesets. `shell: bash` already fails the step
      # on a non-zero exit, so no wrapper is needed.
      run: callisto status --check

    - name: Pre-Flight Release Plan Simulation (DAG Pre-Check)
      shell: bash
      env:
        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
      run: |
        echo "::group::Simulating Release Plan"
        callisto release --dry-run --format text
        echo "::endgroup::"

    - name: Render PR Release Pre-Flight Summary
      shell: bash
      env:
        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
      run: |
        echo "### Callisto Release Pre-Flight Verification" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Package Discovery**: All workspace crates and packages are correctly tracked." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Configuration Health**: \`callisto.toml\` schema and rules are valid." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Changeset Integrity**: Pending changesets are valid." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "#### Workspace Package Status" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo '```' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        callisto status >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo '```' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
name: 'Callisto Release-PR Action'
description: 'Creates or updates a Callisto release PR; durable execution belongs to the repository workflow'
inputs:
  version_command:
    description: 'Version command; defaults to callisto version, which refreshes lockfiles. Callisto appends --emit-decision <decision_path>.'
    required: false
    default: 'callisto version'
  decision_path:
    description: 'Path, relative to cwd, where the version command records the exact release decision this PR carries. Committed alongside the manifest and changelog edits; `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` verifies the merged commit against this file rather than re-deriving release policy.'
    required: false
    default: '.callisto/release-decision.json'
  commit_message:
    description: 'Release-PR commit message'
    required: false
    default: 'chore(release): version packages'
  title:
    description: 'Release-PR title'
    required: false
    default: 'chore(release): version packages'
  pr_label:
    description: 'Release-PR label'
    required: false
    default: 'callisto: release'
  setup_git_user:
    description: 'Unused no-op, kept for backward compatibility. The managed branch is committed through the forge commit API, not a local `git commit`, so no Git identity is ever configured.'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  branch:
    description: 'Base branch for the release PR'
    required: false
    default: 'main'
  release_branch:
    description: 'Branch managed for the release PR'
    required: false
    default: 'callisto/version-packages'
  github_token:
    description: 'Optional GitHub token for pull-request and forge commit API operations. The managed branch is never pushed with `git push`; the default GITHUB_TOKEN is sufficient even on a public repository, since the executor never writes `.github/workflows/*`.'
    required: false
    default: ''
  setup_callisto:
    description: 'Install the Callisto environment before running'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  version:
    description: >-
      Version tag of Callisto to install. Default 'latest' installs the release this action's own
      invocation is pinned to (github.action_ref resolved against callisto@ tags), falling back to
      the newest published release when that ref is unset or unresolvable.
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  cwd:
    description: 'Workspace directory'
    required: false
    default: '.'
  mode:
    description: 'version-pr (default): create/update the release PR. release: run `callisto release`.'
    required: false
    default: 'version-pr'
outputs:
  hasChangesets:
    description: 'Whether pending changesets were found (mode: version-pr only)'
    value: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}
  published:
    description: 'Whether `callisto release` published anything (mode: release only; otherwise false)'
    value: ${{ steps.release.outputs.published || 'false' }}
  publishedPackages:
    description: 'JSON array of packages `callisto release` published (mode: release only; otherwise [])'
    value: ${{ steps.release.outputs.publishedPackages || '[]' }}
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Validate mode
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_MODE: ${{ inputs.mode }}
      run: bash "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/scripts/validate-mode.sh"
    # setup-callisto's own steps, called directly rather than through its
    # `uses:` (both `$/` and an external owner/repo/path@ref resolve against
    # whichever ref invoked *this* action, not necessarily a real one -- see
    # setup-callisto/scripts/install-callisto.sh's header). github.action_path
    # is this action's own checked-out directory, so a sibling-relative path
    # always uses the same ref this action itself was invoked at.
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      if: inputs.setup_callisto == 'true'
      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Installs or builds the Callisto binary. Factored out of action.yml so
# callisto-action's own environment setup can call it directly by path
# (github.action_path has no ref-ambiguous `uses:` to resolve), instead of
# duplicating this logic.
set -euo pipefail

# Install into $RUNNER_TEMP so the binary never lands inside the workspace
# tree (preventing accidental git-staging by downstream steps that run
# "git add -A").
CALLISTO_BIN_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-bin"
mkdir -p "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
TAG_NAME="$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION"
SOURCE="$INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE"

if [[ "$SOURCE" != "auto" && "$SOURCE" != "local" ]]; then
  echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto source '$SOURCE' (expected auto or local)"
  exit 1
fi

# With no explicit version override, install the release this action's own
# invocation is pinned to (GITHUB_ACTION_REF, github.action_ref) rather than
# whatever is newest, so `callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@X.Y.Z` always
# installs X.Y.Z. Falls back to true "latest" when the ref is unset (local or
# unpinned invocation) or matches no published callisto@ tag. A named ref such
# as the floating `v1` tag stands for the commit it points at.
if [[ "$SOURCE" == "auto" && "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" && -n "${GITHUB_ACTION_REF:-}" ]]; then
  remote_tags=$(git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git 'callisto@*' "$GITHUB_ACTION_REF" 2>/dev/null) || true
  ref_commit=$(printf '%s\n' "$remote_tags" \
    | awk -v ref="refs/tags/$GITHUB_ACTION_REF" '$2 == ref || $2 == ref "^{}" { sha = $1 } END { print sha }')
  resolved_tag=$(printf '%s\n' "$remote_tags" \
    | awk -v ref="${ref_commit:-$GITHUB_ACTION_REF}" '$1 == ref && $2 ~ /^refs\/tags\/callisto@/ { print $2 }' \
    | sed -e 's#^refs/tags/##' -e 's/\^{}$//' \
    | sort -V | tail -n1) || true
  if [[ -n "$resolved_tag" ]]; then
    echo "Resolved action ref $GITHUB_ACTION_REF to $resolved_tag"
    TAG_NAME="$resolved_tag"
  fi
fi

# Validate verification mode
VERIFICATION="${INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION:-fallback}"
case "$VERIFICATION" in
  require|fallback|skip) ;;
  *)
    echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto verification '$VERIFICATION' (valid values: require, fallback, skip)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# Detect OS platform architecture for pre-built binaries
OS_NAME=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
ARCH_NAME=$(uname -m)

if [[ "$OS_NAME" == "darwin" ]]; then
  case "$ARCH_NAME" in
    arm64) ASSET_NAME="callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz" ;;
    x86_64) ASSET_NAME="callisto-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz" ;;
    *) ASSET_NAME="" ;;
  esac
elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == "linux" ]]; then
  case "$ARCH_NAME" in
    x86_64) ASSET_NAME="callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz" ;;
    aarch64 | arm64) ASSET_NAME="callisto-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz" ;;
    *) ASSET_NAME="" ;;
  esac
elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == *"mingw"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"msys"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"windows"* ]]; then
  ASSET_NAME=""
else
  ASSET_NAME=""
fi

if [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" && "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]]; then
  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/latest/download/$ASSET_NAME"
elif [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" ]]; then
  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/download/$TAG_NAME/$ASSET_NAME"
fi

# Derive a crates.io version spec from TAG_NAME: "latest" installs
# whatever crates.io resolves as latest (no --version flag); an
# explicit tag ("callisto@0.5.0" or legacy "callisto-cli@0.5.0")
# strips either prefix down to the bare semver cargo install expects.
CRATE_VERSION="${TAG_NAME#callisto@}"; CRATE_VERSION="${CRATE_VERSION#callisto-cli@}"

# Pick a download destination whose extension matches ASSET_NAME
# (under $RUNNER_TEMP, never the workspace) so the extraction step
# below always has an archive it can actually open -- a hardcoded
# ".tar.gz" path here previously masked the fact that Windows assets
# are zip files, since tar -xzf can't read a zip regardless of what
# the file on disk is really named.
case "$ASSET_NAME" in
  *.zip)
    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.zip"
    ;;
  *.tar.gz)
    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
    ;;
  *)
    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
    ;;
esac

# A prebuilt asset runs with the job's privileges, so it must carry a
# GitHub attestation from the Callisto release workflow before it is
# extracted. require aborts on failure; fallback discards the asset and
# returns 1 so the crates.io path runs; skip trusts the asset.
verify_asset() {
  local reason=""
  if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "skip" ]]; then
    echo "::warning::verification=skip: $ASSET_NAME was not verified"
    return 0
  fi
  if ! command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    reason="gh is not installed"
  elif ! gh attestation verify "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" \
      --repo orin-dx/callisto \
      --signer-workflow orin-dx/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml \
      --deny-self-hosted-runners; then
    reason="attestation verification failed"
  fi
  [[ -z "$reason" ]] && return 0
  rm -f "$DOWNLOAD_DEST"
  if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "require" ]]; then
    echo "::error::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason (verification=require)"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "::warning::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason; discarding it and installing from crates.io (verification=fallback)"
  return 1
}

# Download, verify and extract the prebuilt asset; nonzero means use the fallback chain.
fetch_prebuilt() {
  curl -sL -f "$DOWNLOAD_URL" -o "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  verify_asset || return 1
  # Extract only the expected binary, never the whole archive.
  case "$ASSET_NAME" in
    *.zip)
      unzip -q "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" callisto.exe -d "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
      ;;
    *)
      tar -xzf "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" -C "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" callisto
      ;;
  esac
}

# Dependencies named callisto-cli do not establish checkout source ownership.
owns_local_source() {
  local workspace git_root metadata
  workspace=$(cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && pwd -P) || return 1
  git_root=$(git -C "$workspace" rev-parse --show-toplevel) || return 1
  [[ "$git_root" == "$workspace" ]] || return 1
  git -C "$workspace" ls-files --error-unmatch -- \
    Cargo.toml crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs >/dev/null || return 1
  metadata=$(cargo metadata --locked --offline --no-deps --format-version 1 \
    --manifest-path "$workspace/Cargo.toml") || return 1
  jq -e --arg workspace "$workspace" '
    .workspace_root == $workspace and
    (.workspace_members as $members | [.packages[] |
      select(.name == "callisto-cli" and .source == null and
        .manifest_path == ($workspace + "/crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml") and
        (.id as $id | $members | index($id) != null) and
        any(.targets[]; .name == "callisto" and (.kind | index("bin") != null) and
          .src_path == ($workspace + "/crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs")))] | length == 1)
  ' <<< "$metadata" >/dev/null
}

if [[ "$SOURCE" == "local" ]]; then
  if ! owns_local_source; then
    echo "::error::setup-callisto source=local requires a Callisto workspace checkout; check out Callisto source or use source=auto"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "Building local callisto binary from current repository commit..."
  cargo build --locked --manifest-path "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/Cargo.toml" -p callisto-cli \
    --bin callisto --target-dir "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target"
  cp "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target/debug/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
elif [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" ]] && fetch_prebuilt; then
  echo "Callisto downloaded from GitHub Releases ($DOWNLOAD_URL)"
elif [[ "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]] && cargo install callisto-cli --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet; then
  echo "Callisto installed from crates.io (latest)"
  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
elif [[ "$TAG_NAME" != "latest" ]] && cargo install callisto-cli --version "$CRATE_VERSION" --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet; then
  echo "Callisto installed from crates.io ($CRATE_VERSION)"
  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
else
  if [[ "$TAG_NAME" != "latest" ]]; then
    echo "::error::callisto $TAG_NAME is available neither as a prebuilt asset nor on crates.io"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "Installing from git source (crates.io install failed or was skipped)..."
  cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git callisto-cli --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet
  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
fi

echo "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" >> $GITHUB_PATH
if [[ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json" ]]; then
  echo "::add-matcher::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json"
fi

      --deny-self-hosted-runners; then
    reason="attestation verification failed"
  fi
  [[ -z "$reason" ]] && return 0
  rm -f "$DOWNLOAD_DEST"
  if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "require" ]]; then
    echo "::error::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason (verification=require)"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "::warning::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason; discarding it and installing from crates.io (verification=fallback)"
  return 1
}

# Download, verify and extract the prebuilt asset; nonzero means use the fallback chain.
fetch_prebuilt() {
  curl -sL -f "$DOWNLOAD_URL" -o "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  verify_asset || return 1
  # Extract only the expected binary, never the whole archive.
  case "$ASSET_NAME" in
    *.zip)
      unzip -q "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" callisto.exe -d "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
      ;;
    *)
      tar -xzf "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" -C "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" callisto
      ;;
  esac
}

# Dependencies named callisto-cli do not establish checkout source ownership.
owns_local_source() {
  local workspace git_root metadata
  workspace=$(cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && pwd -P) || return 1
  git_root=$(git -C "$workspace" rev-parse --show-toplevel) || return 1
  [[ "$git_root" == "$workspace" ]] || return 1
  git -C "$workspace" ls-files --error-unmatch -- \
    Cargo.toml crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs >/dev/null || return 1
  metadata=$(cargo metadata --locked --offline --no-deps --format-version 1 \
    --manifest-path "$workspace/Cargo.toml") || return 1
  jq -e --arg workspace "$workspace" '
    .workspace_root == $workspace and
    (.workspace_members as $members | [.packages[] |
      select(.name == "callisto-cli" and .source == null and
        .manifest_path == ($workspace + "/crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml") and
        (.id as $id | $members | index($id) != null) and
        any(.targets[]; .name == "callisto" and (.kind | index("bin") != null) and
          .src_path == ($workspace + "/crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs")))] | length == 1)
  ' <<< "$metadata" >/dev/null
}

if [[ "$SOURCE" == "local" ]]; then
  if ! owns_local_source; then
    echo "::error::setup-callisto source=local requires a Callisto workspace checkout; check out Callisto source or use source=auto"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "Building local callisto binary from current repository commit..."
  cargo build --locked --manifest-path "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/Cargo.toml" -p callisto-cli \
    --bin callisto --target-dir "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target"
  cp "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target/debug/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
elif [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" ]] && fetch_prebuilt; then
  echo "Callisto downloaded from GitHub Releases ($DOWNLOAD_URL)"
elif [[ "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]] && cargo install callisto-cli --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet; then
  echo "Callisto installed from crates.io (latest)"
  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
elif [[ "$TAG_NAME" != "latest" ]] && cargo install callisto-cli --version "$CRATE_VERSION" --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet; then
  echo "Callisto installed from crates.io ($CRATE_VERSION)"
  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
else
  if [[ "$TAG_NAME" != "latest" ]]; then
    echo "::error::callisto $TAG_NAME is available neither as a prebuilt asset nor on crates.io"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "Installing from git source (crates.io install failed or was skipped)..."
  cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git callisto-cli --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet
  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
fi

echo "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" >> $GITHUB_PATH
if [[ -f "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json" ]]; then
  echo "::add-matcher::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/callisto-problem-matcher.json"
fi

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [__BRANCH__]

permissions: {}

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  version-pr:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: asset-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets

        with:
          name: python-dist
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets
      - name: Write the artifact manifest
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true' || needs.plan.outputs.has_python == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PYTHON: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.has_python }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --artifact-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets"
            --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-manifest.json")
          if [[ "$HAS_PYTHON" == true ]]; then args+=(--seal-python); fi
          callisto release artifact-manifest "${args[@]}"
      - name: Execute the release
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json"
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA")

            args+=(--artifact-manifest "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-manifest.json" --artifact-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets")
          fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local actions are commit-bound by the checkout. Every external GitHub action
# must use its full immutable commit hash; Docker actions must use an immutable
# content digest.
set -euo pipefail

status=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  reference=${line#*uses: }
  reference=${reference%% #*}
  reference=${reference//[[:space:]]/}
  # Workspace-relative and GitHub's self-repository references are bound to
  # local repository content; only external actions need an explicit pin.
  [[ "$reference" == ./* || "$reference" == '$/'* ]] && continue
  if [[ "$reference" == docker://* ]]; then
    valid='^docker://[^@[:space:]]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'
  else
    valid='^[^@[:space:]]+@[0-9a-f]{40}$'
  fi
  if [[ ! "$reference" =~ $valid ]]; then
    printf 'mutable or malformed external action reference: %s\n' "$line" >&2
    status=1
  fi
done < <(rg --no-heading --glob '*.yml' --glob '*.yaml' '^\s*uses:\s*' .github)
codeowners=.github/CODEOWNERS
if [[ ! -f "$codeowners" ]] \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/workflows/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners" \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/actions/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners"; then
  printf 'CODEOWNERS must cover .github/workflows/ and .github/actions/ with a real owner\n' >&2
  status=1
fi
exit "$status"

# Security Policy

## Reporting a Vulnerability

Email **security@orin-dx.com** — don't open a public issue for anything that could be exploited before a fix ships.

Include:
- Which crate or code path is affected
- The concrete failure scenario — what an attacker could do, and how
- Steps to reproduce, if you have them

Expect an acknowledgment within 5 business days. We'll keep you posted as a fix moves through triage, and credit you in the release notes unless you'd rather stay anonymous.

## Scope

Callisto edits manifests and pushes releases across multiple package registries from inside CI, so the threat model is higher-stakes than a typical CLI tool:

- **Registry token exposure** — Callisto's own release workflow (`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`) grants `contents`/`pull-requests` write only to the jobs that need them (`version-pr`, `execute`); registry credentials (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, and `NPM_TOKEN`/`TWINE_PASSWORD` for workspaces that publish npm/PyPI packages) reach only the `execute` job. A way to make Callisto, or the in-repo `.github/actions/callisto-action`, exfiltrate those tokens, or publish to a package other than the one it was asked to, is a critical finding.
- **Workflow/action injection** — Callisto is designed to run unattended on `push` to `main` in downstream repos. An untrusted PR that could get its content executed by the release workflow (rather than merely analyzed) is in scope.
- **Manifest parser safety** — `callisto-manifests` edits `Cargo.toml`/`package.json` via CST-preserving parsers (`toml_edit`, `serde_json`) rather than regex specifically to avoid corruption; a crafted manifest that causes incorrect writes, path traversal, or a crash mid-write (bypassing the atomic `NamedTempFile` + `fs::rename` guarantee) is a real finding.
- **Version/changelog spoofing** — a way to make `callisto version` compute or apply an incorrect bump, or inject arbitrary content into a generated changelog, that a maintainer could plausibly merge without noticing.
- **Git operation safety** — `callisto_model::vcs` runs the system `git` binary; argument injection through ref names or paths, or unsafe handling of an untrusted repository (submodules, refs, hooks), is in scope.

Dependency vulnerabilities are already checked continuously via `just audit` (`cargo deny check advisories`) in CI — a report that only restates an existing advisory `cargo audit`/`cargo deny` already flags isn't a new finding, but a way to bypass or disable that check is.

Out of scope: vulnerabilities in Cargo, npm, PyPI, or GitHub Actions themselves — report those to the respective platform.

## Supported Versions

Security fixes land on `main` and the latest published release of each affected crate. Given Callisto is pre-1.0, older minor versions are not backported — upgrade to the latest release.

81:      "description": "Prints a shell completion script to stdout.",
126:      "criterion": "When stdout is a terminal and NO_COLOR is unset, `status` and `release --dry-run` render a box-drawing table with ANSI colour; when stdout is piped they print plain indented lines with no ANSI codes or box-drawing characters."
134:      "criterion": "CLICOLOR_FORCE or FORCE_COLOR (any value) turns colour and tables on for piped stdout, and CLICOLOR=0 turns them off on a terminal."
142:      "criterion": "With `--format json`, the status, add, init, pre and snapshot reports on stdout are single JSON objects with camelCase keys and a top-level `schemaVersion`, `command` (the subcommand name) and `dryRun`. The status, version, snapshot and matrix reports carry `schemaVersion` 2 and name every package `ecosystem/name` for its primary ecosystem, promoted or not; the other reports carry 1."
146:      "criterion": "When a command fails under `--format json`, stderr ends with a JSON object `{\"schemaVersion\", \"command\", \"error\": {\"code\", \"message\", \"help\", \"path\"}}` and the exit code is 1; `command` is the subcommand that was parsed and `path` is `null` unless the error carries a structured filesystem path.",
151:      "criterion": "When a command fails under text format, stderr shows a diagnostic with an error code and a message, and the exit code is 1.",
161:      "criterion": "`completions <shell>` and `schema` exit 0 without printing an error or panicking when stdout's reading end is already closed (e.g. piped into a command that exits early); a `--format json` report command's write error in that same situation propagates as `E213` and exits 1."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs `callisto release` (mode: release) and fills published/publishedPackages
# from its receipt; callisto release's own idempotency makes a redundant run a no-op.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$INPUT_CWD"

runtime_dir="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/callisto-release.XXXXXX")"
receipt="$runtime_dir/release-receipt.json"
cleanup() {
  rm -f "$runtime_dir/npmrc" "$receipt"
  rmdir "$runtime_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

if [[ -n "${NPM_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
  npm_config="${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-${HOME:-}/.npmrc}"
  if [[ -n "${HOME:-}" && -f "$npm_config" ]]; then
    cp "$npm_config" "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
  else
    : > "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
  printf '\n//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}\n' >> "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
  export CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG="$runtime_dir/npmrc"
fi

if [[ -n "${PYPI_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
  export TWINE_USERNAME=__token__
  export TWINE_PASSWORD="$PYPI_TOKEN"
  unset PYPI_TOKEN
fi

output=$(callisto --format json release --receipt "$receipt")

if jq -e '.nothingToRelease == true' <<< "$output" > /dev/null; then
  echo 'published=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo 'publishedPackages=[]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo '::notice::Nothing to release.'
  exit 0
fi

packages=$(jq -c '[
    .outcomes[]
    | select(.outcome.kind == "published" and (.operation.role.kind == "registryPublish" or .operation.role.kind == "platformPublish"))
    | .operation.package
  ] | unique' "$receipt")
published=$(jq -r 'length > 0' <<< "$packages")
{
  echo "published=$published"
  echo "publishedPackages=$packages"
} >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

Read-only review of /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/smoke-main. Fifteen findings, ranked by severity then effort. I ran `cargo machete` and `cargo deny check bans licenses sources`. `cargo deny` advisories could not run: the sandbox blocks the advisory-db lock. No builds or tests were run.

Not findings (checked):
- Dependabot already covers `github-actions` and `cargo`, and has a 7-day cooldown.
- `deny.toml` has `wildcards = "deny"` and AGPL is not in the allow list.
- `fs2` is not declared anywhere.
- No crate except `callisto-model` has a `[features]` table (its `test-util` feature is the permitted exception).
- Registry URLs must be `https` (`registry_endpoint.rs:87`).
- `unwrap_used` is allowed at workspace level but denied by a second clippy run (`justfile:57-58`).
- The `--help` banner already says "Cargo, npm and Python" (`cli.rs:5`).
- JSON errors on stderr are specified (`docs/specs/cli.json:146`).
- Color forcing with any value of `CLICOLOR_FORCE` is specified (`docs/specs/cli.json:134`).

1. **Checkout credentials stay on disk while publish tools run (high).**
   - Where: `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml:424`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/simple_workflow.tmpl:25`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/matrix_workflow.tmpl:223`.
   - Evidence: the `execute` job (contents: write) checks out with `persist-credentials: true`. The template comments read `# zizmor: ignore[artipacked] tag push needs persisted credentials`.
   - Issue: `runner.rs:52-93` removes `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` from every child except `gh`, but the same token sits in `.git/config` as an `http.extraheader`. `cargo publish` build scripts, npm lifecycle scripts and `python -m build` run with their cwd inside that checkout and can read it. The env stripping gives no protection against them.
   - Fix: use `persist-credentials: false`. Give only the `git push` child the token, for example via `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=http.extraheader`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0` in the env of that one child (`provider/tag.rs:108`).

2. **`cargo publish` compiles the whole dependency tree with `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` in its environment (medium-high).**
   - Where: `runner.rs:84-87` (`"cargo" => &["CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN"]`), `registry_argv.rs:67-72`.
   - Evidence: the argv is `publish --manifest-path … --locked [--registry]`, with no `--no-verify`. The verify step runs every build script and proc-macro of the crate and its dependencies, all inheriting the token. The npm path passes no `--ignore-scripts`, so `prepublishOnly` and `prepack` scripts also see the npm token.
   - Fix: run `cargo package --locked` (verify) without the token, then `cargo publish --no-verify` with it. Add `--ignore-scripts` to npm publish, or run `npm pack` token-free first.

3. **Unhashed `pip install` in jobs that hold registry secrets (medium).**
   - Where: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs:804-812` (`build==1.4.4`, `twine==7.0.0`), `matrix_workflow.tmpl:200` and `:231`.
   - Evidence: `pip install --quiet __TWINE__` pins only the top-level package; `requests`, `urllib3`, `keyring` and the rest float. The venv `bin` is then put on `GITHUB_PATH` for the `execute` job, which holds `TWINE_PASSWORD`.
   - Fix: generate a hashed constraints file and use `pip install --require-hashes`, or use `uv`.

4. **The `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*` variables and other tokens are not stripped, because stripping is a denylist (medium).**
   - Where: `runner.rs:52-63` (`RELEASE_CREDENTIALS`).
   - Evidence: the list has 10 names. It omits `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL`, which are present whenever `id-token: write` is granted (the templates grant it, see finding 12). It also omits `UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN` and `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN`. The last one is redacted by pattern at `registry.rs:247` but never removed from children.
   - Fix: build the child environment from an allowlist (PATH, HOME, LANG, TMPDIR, `CARGO_*` for cargo, and so on). At minimum, drop `ACTIONS_*` and any `*_TOKEN`/`*_PASSWORD`/`*_SECRET` name for non-publisher children, matching the redaction suffix rule at `registry.rs:256`.

5. **Generated-workflow lint tests silently pass when the tools are missing, and CI never installs them (medium).**
   - Where: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init/tests.rs:723-742`.
   - Evidence: `Err(_) => eprintln!("actionlint not installed; skipping that check")`, and the same for zizmor. The CI `test` job (`callisto-ci.yml:101-126`) installs only just and nextest. So `callisto init`'s two workflow templates are never linted in CI.
   - Fix: copy the CI-guard pattern from `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs:283-288`: assert the tool exists when `CI` is set. Add actionlint and zizmor to the test job.

6. **Pins in the generated templates and in composite actions are outside Dependabot and the pin check, and have already drifted (medium).**
   - Where: `crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/matrix_workflow.tmpl:70` (`upload-artifact@043fb46d… # v7.0.1`) and `:196` (`download-artifact@3e5f45b2… # v8.0.1`), against `callisto-release.yml:248` (`@cf430e03… v7.0.2`) and `:313` (`@9000827c… v8.0.2`).
   - Evidence: `.github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh` scans only `*.yml` under `.github`. Dependabot `directory: /` does not scan the composite actions' `uses:` lines (`.github/actions/setup-callisto/action.yml:31` and `:42`, `callisto-action/action.yml:86` and `:97`). It also does not scan `fuzz/Cargo.lock`, whose crate has its own `[workspace]`.
   - Fix: add `directories:` entries for `/.github/actions/*` and a cargo entry for `/fuzz`. Add a test that the template SHAs equal the repo's workflow SHAs.

7. **A timeout kills only the direct child, and no signal handler exists (medium).**
   - Where: `runner.rs:494-497` (`drop(child.kill()); drop(child.wait());`), `main.rs`.
   - Evidence: grep finds no SIGINT, SIGTERM or process-group handling in `crates/*/src`. Children are not put in their own process group.
   - Issue: after a publish timeout, a pnpm/yarn/npm descendant keeps uploading while callisto reports failure. SIGTERM (for example `cancel-in-progress`) kills callisto and orphans the children. The rerun is probably safe, since E235's help says the rerun adopts landed effects, but the state is murky.
   - Fix: spawn with `process_group(0)` and `killpg` on timeout and on SIGINT/SIGTERM. Print "rerun `callisto release execute`; landed effects are adopted" on interrupt.

8. **Nothing in CI packages the crates before release day (medium).**
   - Where: `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml`, `justfile`.
   - Evidence: grep for `cargo package` and `publish --dry-run` in `.github/` and the justfile returns nothing. All five crates carry `readme = "README.md"` whose links are relative (`crates/callisto-cli/README.md:5` → `../../ARCHITECTURE.md`, `../../README.md`), which 404 on crates.io. `callisto-model/src/lib.rs:234` has a test-only `include_str!("../../../docs/errors.md")` that fails when tests run from the crates.io tarball.
   - Fix: add a `cargo package --workspace --locked --allow-dirty` job (or per crate, in dependency order). Use absolute GitHub URLs in the READMEs.

9. **No timeouts anywhere in the main CI, and no per-test timeout (medium-low).**
   - Where: `callisto-ci.yml` (no `timeout-minutes` on any of its 11 jobs), `callisto-advisories.yml`, no `.config/nextest.toml`.
   - Evidence: the 360-minute default applies. Your notes record that gpgsign hangs last about 120s per test. There are 98 direct `Command::new("git")` calls in test code. Some ignore the exit status: `callisto-graph/src/commands/version/tests.rs:42-57` (`commit_all` and `tag` use `.output().expect(..)` and never check `status`), and `:35-38` is the same. A failed commit then silently produces a wrong baseline.
   - Fix: add `timeout-minutes` to every job. Add `.config/nextest.toml` with `slow-timeout = { period = "60s", terminate-after = 3 }`. Route test git through one hermetic helper that sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and asserts success (`callisto-model/src/vcs/tests.rs:29-35` already does this).

10. **Several user-facing diagnostics have a code but no help (medium-low; invariant 4).**
    - Where: `callisto-model/src/format/changeset/mod.rs:62-92` (E042 to E047: `#[diagnostic(code(E042))]` with no help), `callisto-graph/src/changelog/error.rs:6-20` (E060 to E063), `callisto-model/src/format/bump.rs:301-313` (E035 to E039).
    - Related: `PreJsonError` (`format/pre.rs:257-281`) has no `Diagnostic` at all. `CliError::PreJson` (`error.rs:107-112`) wraps every variant in one generic E212 help.
    - Issue: these are the errors a user hits when hand-editing a changeset.
    - Fix: add per-variant help text. Add a test that every top-level diagnostic variant has both code and help.

11. **Unused dependencies, and no CI check for them (low).**
    - Where: `crates/callisto-manifests/Cargo.toml:20` (`camino`) and `:25` (`thiserror`). `cargo machete` reports both as unused, and a grep of that crate's `src` for either name returns nothing.
    - Evidence: `machete` exists only as a manual recipe (`justfile:107-109`) and is not in CI.
    - Related: `Cargo.toml:32` enables `miette` with `features = ["fancy"]` workspace-wide, so the MIT library crate `callisto-model` (`Cargo.toml:31`) pulls in the terminal-rendering stack. `cargo deny` also warns about duplicate `syn` and `unicode-width`.
    - Fix: remove the two dependencies. Add `cargo machete` to CI. Enable `fancy` only in `callisto-cli`.

12. **Generated workflows are looser than the repo's own release workflow (low-medium).**
    - Where: `simple_workflow.tmpl:22` (`permissions: {contents: write, id-token: write}`), `matrix_workflow.tmpl:101` and `:220`.
    - Evidence: `id-token: write` is granted, but OIDC is not implemented (known), so it is pure exposure. Neither template has `timeout-minutes`. The simple template's `version-pr` job has no concurrency group, while its `release` job (`:21`) does. Neither template has a workflow-level group, so two quick pushes race on the same release branch.
    - Fix: drop `id-token` until OIDC lands. Add `concurrency: {group: callisto-version-pr, cancel-in-progress: false}` and per-job `timeout-minutes`.

13. **E157's rerun guidance is CI-centric and omits artifact expiry (low).**
    - Where: `callisto-graph/src/error.rs:379-388` ("Re-run the failed job … do not regenerate the release intent").
    - Evidence: `callisto-release.yml:253-257` and `:342-346` keep the intent and build artifacts for 7 days. After that, "re-run the failed job" cannot work. The `workflow_dispatch` input `release_source_sha` (`:8-11`) is the recovery path, and the help text does not mention it. A local `callisto release` run has no "job" to re-run.
    - Fix: say "re-run `callisto release execute`; after the artifacts expire, dispatch the Release workflow with `release_source_sha`".

14. **The installer's download and fallback steps are weaker than its attestation check (low).**
    - Where: `.github/actions/setup-callisto/scripts/install-callisto.sh:133` and `:190`.
    - Evidence: `curl -sL -f "$DOWNLOAD_URL" -o … 2>/dev/null` has no `--proto '=https' --tlsv1.2`, and it hides curl errors. Line 190 falls back to `cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git` with no `--rev` or `--tag`, which is an unattested mutable HEAD. Line 194 has an unquoted `>> $GITHUB_PATH`.
    - Fix: add `--proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 --retry 3` and keep the stderr. Drop the git fallback, or pin it to a tag.

15. **CLI flag-design wart (low).**
    - Where: `cli.rs:19-31` (global `--dry-run`), `cli.rs:36-41` (`--workflow` and `--no-workflow`).
    - Evidence: the global `--dry-run` is rejected at runtime by four release subcommands (E216, E217, E218, E309). `--workflow` and `--no-workflow` are mutually exclusive but checked by hand (E242) instead of with clap `conflicts_with`.
    - Fix: use `conflicts_with`. Hide or reject `--dry-run` per subcommand through clap rather than runtime errors.
